conditions: T=n.s. (ambient); pH=9.00..9.50; I=n.s. (10 mM carbonate buffer); solvent=water; phase=ACC I (more stable; calcite-like short-range order proposed); surface=none (homogeneous)
method: experiment: constant-pH titration with Ca-ISE, post-nucleation plateau of free ion product
notes: Original Gebauer 2008 determination behind the Day 1 compilation TC-039. Printed as about 3.1 x 10-8 M2; log10 = -7.51. Averaged over three runs, no uncertainty stated. Open copy is an OCR scan from the university repository. Concentration-based product (no activity correction stated in main text).

conditions: T=n.s. (ambient); pH=9.75..10.0; I=n.s. (10 mM carbonate buffer); solvent=water; phase=ACC II (less stable; vaterite-like short-range order proposed); surface=none (homogeneous)
method: experiment: constant-pH titration with Ca-ISE, post-nucleation plateau of free ion product
notes: Second ACC form of Gebauer 2008; log10 = -7.42. Same group and method as TG-001; about one order of magnitude below Brecevic-Nielsen (TC-037/TC-038) and Clarkson (TC-041) values.

conditions: T=n.s.; pH=9.00; I=n.s. (10 mM carbonate buffer plus dosed CaCl2; activity coefficients from initial ionic strength); solvent=water; phase=pc-ACC (proto-calcite); surface=none (homogeneous)
method: experiment: constant-pH potentiometric titration, post-nucleation plateau, mean-activity correction (approach 1)
notes: Table 1 prints 2.90 ± 0.53 in a column headed Ksp [x10-8 M2]; value here is that entry times 1e-8. Error is propagated electrode calibration uncertainty. Ideal evaluation 2.95 ± 0.19; individual-activity approach 2.32 ± 0.41 (TG-005). log10 about -7.54. Same group as Gebauer 2008 (TG-001), independent data set with activity treatment.

conditions: T=n.s.; pH=10.0; I=n.s. (10 mM carbonate buffer plus dosed CaCl2); solvent=water; phase=pv-ACC (proto-vaterite); surface=none (homogeneous)
method: experiment: constant-pH potentiometric titration, post-nucleation plateau, mean-activity correction (approach 1)
notes: Table 1 prints 3.31 ± 0.60 in the column headed Ksp [x10-8 M2]; value here is that entry times 1e-8. log10 about -7.48. Authors: free ion products never reach 4.0e-7 M2, so Brecevic-Nielsen-type ACC cannot form in these dilute runs; they attribute the higher literature values to polyamorphism or to a stabiliser used in earlier work.

conditions: T=n.s.; pH=9.00; I=n.s. (10 mM carbonate buffer plus dosed CaCl2); solvent=water; phase=pc-ACC (proto-calcite); surface=none (homogeneous)
method: experiment: constant-pH potentiometric titration, post-nucleation plateau, individual-ion activity correction (approach 2)
notes: Table 1 prints 2.32 ± 0.41 in the column headed Ksp [x10-8 M2]; value here is that entry times 1e-8. Lowest of the three activity treatments; shows the spread due to activity convention (2.32 to 2.95 at pH 9).

conditions: T=24.5 C ± 0.5; pH=n.s. in main text (MgCl2-NaHCO3 buffered); I=0.17 M ± 0.02; solvent=water; phase=synthetic ACC Ca0.98Mg0.02CO3·nH2O (n 0.4-0.8 for the series); surface=n.s.

notes: Independent group from Gebauer and Kellermeier; agrees with Brecevic-Nielsen -6.39 and is about 1.3 log units above the titration-onset values TG-001 to TG-005. Contains 2.2 mol% Mg at steady state, hence B. Uncertainty as printed (spread of time points). Activity of water taken as unity.

conditions: T=24.5 C ± 0.5; pH=n.s.; I=0.17 M; solvent=water; phase=Mg-free ACC endmember of the ACMC series; surface=n.s.
method: experiment: linear regression of log IAP vs Mg content (this study, Brecevic-Nielsen 1989 and Purgstaller earlier ACMC data)
notes: Intercept of log IAP = 0.0174 x [Mg] - 6.278 (R2 = 0.98); a fitted model value that includes the Brecevic-Nielsen point, hence C and not fully independent of TC-037/TC-038. Also printed in the abstract as -6.28 ± 0.05.

conditions: T=24.5 C ± 0.5; pH=n.s.; I=0.17 M; solvent=water; phase=amorphous Ca(1-x)Mg(x)CO3·nH2O; surface=n.s.
method: experiment: linear regression of log IAP vs Mg content of the amorphous solid
notes: Solubility of ACMC rises 0.0174 log units per mol% Mg, attributed to more structural water and changed short-range order. Relevant if Mg is present in slurry water.

conditions: T=n.s. (DSC scan); pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=none (solid); phase=nominally anhydrous amorphous Ca0.95Mg0.05CO3 (pre-dried 250 C) to crystalline; surface=n.s.
method: experiment: conventional DSC crystallisation exotherm
notes: Printed as enthalpy of crystallisation 156.6 ± 9 J/g (exothermic, sign added here). Enthalpy, not free energy. Authors note it lies within error of anhydrous ACC to calcite (Radha 2010, TC-029). Hydrous precursor held 0.509 mol H2O per mol.

value: ACC solubility set mainly by Mg content; bulk value concurs with established values
conditions: T=n.s.; pH=n.s.; I=n.s.; solvent=water; phase=Ca-rich and Mg-rich ACC with distinct short-range order; surface=n.s.
method: experiment: solubility product from super- and undersaturated runs, in situ PDF, TGA, ICP-OES
notes: Independent group (Mergelsberg et al. 2020). Two short-range structures selected by carbonate activity; numbers not in the abstract and the full text was unreachable (repository host timed out).

conditions: T=298.15 K assumed (not stated in main text); pH=9.00; I=activity-corrected; solvent=water; phase=pc-ACC vs calcite; surface=n.s.

notes: Derived: RT ln10 x (log Ksp ACC - log Ksp calcite) = 5.708 kJ/mol x (-7.538 + 8.48) with Ksp(pc-ACC) = 2.90e-8 (TG-003) and log Ksp(calcite) = -8.48 (Day 1, 10.1073/pnas.1312369111). Per CaCO3 with water activity 1. Less than half the Brecevic-Nielsen-based 11.9 kJ/mol (TC-030/TC-031).

conditions: T=24.5 C; pH=n.s.; I=0.17 M (activity basis); solvent=water; phase=ACC with 2.2 mol% Mg vs calcite; surface=n.s.
method: compilation: derived from primary ACC IAP and compiled calcite Ksp
notes: Derived: 5.708 kJ/mol x (-6.20 + 8.48) = 13.0 kJ/mol, with log IAP(ACC) = -6.20 (TG-006) and log Ksp(calcite) = -8.48 (Day 1, 10.1073/pnas.1312369111). Water activity taken as 1 as in the source.

conditions: T=n.s. (ambient); pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=none (dried powder); phase=synthetic ACC CaCO3·1.1H2O (n = 1.1 ± 0.03 by TGA); surface=n.s.
method: experiment: Ar-gas pycnometry
notes: Printed 2.282(2) g/cm3; uncertainty is last-digit uncertainty as printed. Water content from TGA in the same work. Read from the open accepted manuscript (repository copy). Much denser than the 1.62 g/cm3 of in situ SAXS (TC-054/TC-055).

conditions: T=n.s. (ambient); pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=none (dried powder); phase=partially dehydrated ACC CaCO3·0.5H2O (heat treated); surface=n.s.
method: experiment: Ar-gas pycnometry
notes: Printed 2.428(2) g/cm3. Densification on dehydration. Heat-treated sample hence B for P0 (aqueous ACC is more hydrated).

conditions: T=n.s. (ambient); pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=none; phase=ACC CaCO3·1.1H2O; surface=n.s.
method: experiment: derived from pycnometric density and TGA water content
notes: Derived: M = 100.087 + 1.1 x 18.015 = 119.90 g/mol; V_m = 119.90 / 2.282 = 52.54 cm3 per mol CaCO3, structural water INCLUDED. For comparison calcite is about 36.9 cm3/mol. The share attributable to CaCO3 alone is not separable from these data.

conditions: T=n.s. (ambient); pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=none; phase=partially dehydrated ACC CaCO3·0.5H2O; surface=n.s.
method: experiment: derived from pycnometric density and TGA water content
notes: Derived: M = 100.087 + 0.5 x 18.015 = 109.09 g/mol; V_m = 109.09 / 2.428 = 44.93 cm3 per mol CaCO3, structural water INCLUDED. Difference to TG-015 (7.6 cm3 for 0.6 H2O) is below the 10.8 cm3 of 0.6 mol liquid water, consistent with densification.

conditions: T=n.s.; pH=n.s.; I=n.s.; solvent=n.s.; phase=ACC endmember of amorphous Ca/Sr carbonate series (water content not given in abstract); surface=n.s.
method: experiment: SAXS, PDF, TGA, ICP-MS
notes: Independent group (Mergelsberg et al. 2024). Lower than the pycnometric 2.282 for n = 1.1 (TG-013); water content needed for a molar volume is in the paywalled full text. Abstract states molar volumes are additive in water content.

conditions: T=n.s.; pH=n.s.; I=n.s.; solvent=water; phase=ACC nanoparticles 66-196 nm; surface=ACC-solution
method: experiment: size dependence of apparent ACC solubility (Gibbs-Thomson type analysis)
notes: Printed as about 0.33 J/m2; an order of magnitude above the Day 1 rows TC-024 (10.2 mJ/m2) and TC-025 (14-25 mJ/m2). Abstract only (full text paywalled); the solubility model, water content and hydration of the particle surface are not visible, so the number may include non-interfacial size effects.

conditions: T=n.s.; pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=none; phase=calcite; surface=bulk
method: compilation: experimental value quoted in a DFT paper
notes: Quoted for comparison by Medeiros et al. 2007; original experiment not named in the abstract (likely an electron spectroscopy measurement). Indirect DFT gaps in the same work are lower (LDA/GGA underestimate). Other work cited in later literature places the optical gap nearer 7.1-7.5 eV, unverified here.

conditions: T=n.s. (ambient); pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=n.s. (UV-vis of dispersed powder); phase=CaCO3 nanoparticles from industrial waste (polymorph and impurities per XRD/EDX in source); surface=n.s.
method: experiment: UV-vis absorption maximum at 206 nm converted with E = hc/lambda
notes: Estimated, hence C: the absorption maximum is not an absorption edge, and 206 nm sits near the instrument cut-off. Tauc indirect fit said to be close. Agrees with the 6.0 eV of TG-019.

locator: pdf p. 1, abstract and pdf p. 2 (Fig. 2 discussion)
symbol: Phi0 x s^2 (Phi0 = 2.5 eV / s^2 with s in nm)
conditions: T=4.2 K (spectra); pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=none; phase=native amorphous AlOx grown in O2 at room temperature to saturation; surface=Al/AlOx/(Al; Cu; Au; Nb) planar junctions
method: experiment: Simmons-model fit of tunnel conductance spectra (epsilon = 4)
notes: PROXY for a CaCO3 tunnel barrier (no CaCO3 tunnelling data found). Model-fit barrier heights fall as 1/s^2, i.e. about 8.6 eV at 0.54 nm and about 2 eV near 1.1 nm; authors say Phi0 is unrelated to the bulk Al2O3 gap. Preprint of Gloos, Koppinen, Pekola.

conditions: T=n.s. (oxidation at room temperature); pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=none (pure O2); phase=native AlOx at saturation; surface=Al base electrode
method: experiment: barrier widths from tunnel spectra (Simmons fit) histogram
notes: PROXY context: saturated native oxide widths come in steps of 0.38(5) nm (one O layer); pure-Al base electrodes mostly gave the next width s1 (s0 plus one 0.38 nm step). Sets the thickness of the native tunnel barrier beneath any CaCO3 layer.

conditions: T=n.s.; pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=none; phase=AlOx 5-15 nm in metal-oxide-semiconductor structures; surface=metal/AlOx
method: compilation: internal photoemission value quoted by Gloos et al. (their ref. 17)
notes: PROXY. Same passage quotes 3.90(3) eV from ballistic electron emission spectroscopy for 8 nm AlOx (ref. 16) and 4.25(5) eV for SiO2 by photoemission. Thick-film values far above the thin-junction fits of TG-021.

conditions: T=4.2 K; pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=none; phase=thermally grown AlOx in Al-AlOx-Al junctions (25 nm Al films); surface=Al/AlOx
method: experiment: differential conductance below 0.17 V fitted with trapezoidal WKB barrier (phi, transition width, barrier width, m* free)
notes: PROXY. Same fit: barrier width 8.43 Angstrom, transition region 1.70 Angstrom, effective mass 0.29 m_e. Closest to DFT Al-terminated interfaces (TG-025).

symbol: phi (DFT Schottky barrier; mean of six interfaces)
conditions: T=0 K (DFT); pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=none; phase=crystalline alpha-Al2O3 slab on Al(111); surface=six Al/Al2O3 stacking and termination variants
method: computation: DFT (PBE) valence band offset plus experimental Al2O3 gap 8.8 eV
notes: PROXY. Spread up to 2 eV between geometries; Al-terminated mean 2.32 eV, O-terminated mean 1.42 eV. Uses an experimental gap of 8.8 eV for Al2O3 (cited).

conditions: T=4.2 K; pH=n.a.; I=n.a.; solvent=none; phase=thermally grown AlOx; surface=Al/AlOx/Al
method: experiment: derived from fitted WKB barrier height and effective mass
notes: PROXY, derived: kappa = sqrt(2 m* phi)/hbar = 5.123 nm^-1 x sqrt(0.29 x 2.56) = 4.41 nm^-1; transmission falls as exp(-2 kappa d), 2 kappa = 8.83 nm^-1 (one decade per 0.26 nm). Inputs phi = 2.56 eV and m* = 0.29 m_e printed on pdf p. 7. Rectangular-barrier estimate; ignores image forces.
